When a child or individual is diagnosed with Niemann-Pick disease it adversely affects the whole family. Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia - heart rhythm disturbance. It occurs when chaotic electrical activity develops in the upper chambers of the heart (the atria). As a result, the atria no longer beat in an organised, regular rhythm, so the patient's pulse is irregular and as a result, the pumping of the heart is less efficient. Across the UK approximately 1.2 million people suffer with Atrial Fibrillation.

Special needs Community Information Point - SCIP:  
SCIP is the database for children and young people aged birth to 25 years who have special needs or a disability and their families in Cambridgeshire. 

This is a free service offered to families in Cambridgeshire.

SCIP is used to get information to families.
·	Do you ever find yourself stuck and not know where to go to get information or advice? 
·	Do you find yourself out of the loop – everyone seems to have the information before you do!
SCIP may have the answer!

Email Network and Information Requests:  
SCIP provides information to families on events, activities, general information and much more. Families can request information from SCIP. If you need help to find a support group, a hairdresser who has experience of children with special needs; information on grants, transport, tutors, youth clubs in your area – anything – just ask and SCIP can help. 

Through the SCIP Email Network you have easy access to a wealth of experience and knowledge. 

SCIP Card:  
The Card was developed following requests from families who on occasion need assistance while out with their child, especially where the condition is not visibly evident, when a child is likely to react to a situation such as loud noises or is in an uncomfortable situation and may react in a way that draws attention. It can be used as proof of disability/additional need for access to disabled toilets or where concessions are available for people with a disability. More information about the Card is available on the website.

You must join the SCIP Database to be eligible for a SCIP Card and to receive information through the Email Network.

Activity Passport:  
This booklet has been produced to help provide essential information about a child when they are going to an activity such as scouts, play schemes, organised activities, etc. The Passport can hold information about a child’s medication, likes and dislikes, and emergency contacts. More information about the Activity Passport is available on the SCIP website.

To Join SCIP:  
If you would like to join SCIP and apply for a SCIP Card, please complete the online form here: www.cambridgeshire.gov.uk/scip

We can complete this task for you/the person you care for via post or in person if you would prefer.Third Party Supported AccountSome people are not able to manage their own care funds (or would prefer not to).  We can do this for you through our Third Party Supported Account (TPSA) Service.  The money from the individual's care package (i.e. the direct payment plus other funding) is received by Penderels Trust.  We will pay all the agreed bills for care (e.g. care agency invoices or staff wages) from the money we hold on their behalf.  They still have responsibility for their own money.Additional Living Support PackagesIt may be that the person you care for requires additional living support services to ensure they are able to get the most out of their direct payment package.  We have a number of options offering a higher level of support (over and above the basic telephone support); we would discuss with you/the person you care for which would be most appropriate for their needs.Payroll ServicesThe Penderels Trust Payroll Bureau offers a specialist service for people who employ their own personal assistant or carer.  Our service includes processing timesheets, issuing payslips, liaison with HMRC, calculation of sick pay and maternity pay, production of P60s and P45s, electronic submission of end-of-year returns to HMRC and calculation of quarterly payments to be made to HMRC.  We also offer a BACS service where we pay staff wages directly into their bank account and make your quarterly payment to HMRC on your behalf.Peer Support GroupThe peer support group is an informal group of people who use Penderels Trust's services that meet on a regular basis; their carers are welcome to join them.  The peer support group is run by the people who use our services, not by Penderels Trust themselves.  They meet regularly to discuss issues around direct payments, the service we provide them and how we can move these services forward.  The group also invites other people and organisations to talk to them about relevant topics or simply to entertain them.

Both professional and self referral.  We support individuals referred to us via the local authority (usually via a social worker) and we support those who are self-funding. Individuals who wish to consider taking a direct payment (or are enquiring on behalf of someone else) should speak to their social services department in the first instance.  Individuals who receive no funding but wish to access support can contact Penderels Trust directly.

Carers’ Hub supports unpaid carers living in Lambeth or caring for someone who lives in the Borough. We work directly with young carers from the age of 5  upwards and adult carers, providing tailored 1-2-1 support, social and wellbeing activities, peer support groups tailored to dementia, mental health, learning disability and young carers.  We also deliver first aid training and provide free legal clinics through our partnerships, and run the Lambeth Carers Card scheme which connects carers to information and resources to support their caring role.

We run a mix of peer support groups, coffee mornings and social activities each month, allowing you to share your experience of caring, make friends, and develop new skills. The Cheshire Asbestos Victims Support Group was formed in 1992, by members who had been actively involved in campaign issues, relating to asbestos, since the early 1980’s. The group gained Charity Status in 1994.

The group changed its direction from campaign work to support work for victims of asbestos related disease and their families. The intention was to ensure that all those that were affected by asbestos diseases, in Cheshire, had access to help, information, advice and support. It was felt that if victims were encouraged to pursue claims for their illness then this would help to improve their quality of life and make asbestos uninsurable thus adding weight to the fight for an asbestos ban. The group still actively campaign on many issues involving asbestos victims and their families. In 1999 the UK eventually banned the import and use of asbestos.
